blocks.x: For as contentious as the Star Wars sequel trilogy is, it did at least provide the franchise with one of its most enduring modern characters in Kylo Ren. A standout performance by Adam Driver helped elevate the villain to greatness by capturing his emotional depth as the son of Han Solo and Leia Organa, who turned to the dark side and became the supreme leader of the First Order. From his final confrontation with his father to his monologues, his wrestling with his actions and whether to return to the light, and ultimately a redemption arc that cost him his life but saved his family legacy, all the pieces were in place to construct a layered antagonist worthy of following up the legendary Darth Vader. Yet, there's so much left untold about the character that has only more recently been addressed in the comics.

Famed Daredevil writer Charles Soule has done much to help Ben Solo reach his full potential by fleshing out his story on the page. In 2019, he penned the limited series The Rise of Kylo Ren from Marvel Comics, depicting his fall to the Dark Side and rebirth as Kylo Ren under Supreme Leader Snoke with the Knights of Ren. It showed how even the Light's greatest hope was not safe from the claws of evil, slowly and insidiously pushing him down the wrong path. Before that, The Legacy of Vader forced the Skywalkers to wrestle with his actions and legacy as a grandson of Anakin. Most recently, though, Soule has returned to the time between The Last Jedi and The Rise of Skywalker with The Fall of Kylo Ren, showing how the villain forged his own path of tyranny. In jumping around the Star Wars sequel timeline, he's gotten a chance from Marvel and Lucasfilm to answer the burning questions that ate at him after seeing the films himself.

In an interview with Collider's Maggie Lovitt at FanX Salt Lake City over the weekend, Soule described how his process in tackling Star Wars' staple characters often revolves around the questions he wants to see answered about them as a fan. "Whenever I get one of these chances to expand the story of a really well-known character in Star Wars — right now, we're talking about Kylo Ren, but I've also gotten to do it with Darth Vader and Luke Skywalker, all kinds of big characters in the mythos, which is a blast. I feel very honored to be able to do it," he said. "Usually, I start with trying to figure out if there's actually a story to tell, and for me, that begins with the questions that the films and maybe TV shows don't answer." For The Fall of Kylo Ren, those questions involved the character's mindset after burning down many of the connections to his old life and reflecting on everything he's lost with his despicable acts.

"With Kylo Ren, in particular, for me, it was a really interesting set of stories to be told based around the moments right after Episode VIII, when he becomes the supreme leader of the First Order, but he's kind of lost everything. He's killed his dad, he's met Rey, he's had this confrontation with Luke Skywalker. All these things have happened in a very short period of time, because Episodes VII and VIII take place over, I don't know, a week or two. So all of these life-changing things for this young man, to me, it felt like there was a ton of rich story ground to cover."
